item.title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.26673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.
item.dc:creator: Cyril B\'en\'ezet, Cyril Nefzaoui-Blanchard, Sergio Pulido

item.title: Reconstructing risk preferences from data
item.description: arXiv:2611.27692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of reconstructing risk preferences from data. Specifically, for a finite dataset consisting of contingent claims and their evaluations, we aim at reconstructing a risk measure that is finite-valued, cash-additive, convex, and Lipschitz continuous. Our first result establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for a dataset to be compatible with a risk measure, that is the evaluations are stemming from a risk measure applied to the contingent claims. Our second result provides a reconstruction formula for compatible datasets, which we term \emph{universal risk measure}. We further extend the reconstruction to monotone risk measures and establish sharp Lipschitz constants for both general and monotone reconstructions. We further show that we explicitly reconstruct linear preferences and evaluations by the Expected Shortfall. We conclude with a numerical application to European options.
item.dc:creator: Anastasis Kratsios, Silvana M. Pesenti, Philipp Zimmermann

item.title: Capturing cash non-additivity and horizon risk via BSDEs and generalized shortfall
item.description: arXiv:2603.14024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whenever dealing with horizons of different times scales, risk evaluation of losses may incur in both interest rate uncertainty and horizon risk as introduced in [11]. With the goal to capture both effects, we work with cash subadditive fully-dynamic risk measures. In this work we consider such measures obtained via the BSDE and the shortfall approaches. We stress that we consider BSDEs both with Lipschitz and quadratic drivers. We then introduce the hq-entropic risk measure on losses as an effective example of fully-dynamic risk measure serving the scope. Shortfall risk measures are extended to capture cash non-additivity. For our newly introduced h-generalized shortfall risk measures we provide a dual representation and we connect them to fully-dynamic certainty equivalent. To conclude, we can see that the hq-entropic risk measures on losses belong to the family h-generalized shortfall, but they are not of certainty equivalent type. We note that the classical entropic risk measure, besides being generated by a BSDE, is also both a shortfall and a certainty equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Di Nunno, Emanuela Rosazza Gianin
